conviction_note: abs_move 16 (event-implied 15.1%, own median 10.4% but four of eight prints above 15%, thin coverage, 16% of float short) times a 58% up lean resting on a company that has beaten its own revenue guide or consensus four straight quarters and signed post-guide embedded deals (Merge Labs inside Q3), offset by a core business growing ~2% and a guided EBITDA step-down; impact_sum 3.2 and impact_scaled 2.56 agree in sign and roughly in size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide $26-30M (midpoint $28M) from the Q2 release 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001804176/000180417626000025/bfly-20260730xexx991.htm ; estimates $28.8M (Benzinga, https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/BFLY/earnings-forecasts) and $29.9M (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/BFLY), EPS -$0.04/-$0.05. Sized against ~$29M. FY guide $119-123M with H1 = $59.1M, so implied H2 $59.9-63.9M and implied Q4 ~$30-38M.
positioning_check: Short interest 33.59M shares, 16.2% of float, 6.2 days to cover, settlement 2026-10-15 (published 2026-10-26), up 6.2% from 31.64M on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/BFLY/short-interest/). Baseline: 25d skew -1.92 vol pts (calls slightly bid), put/call OI 0.16 (very call-heavy), event-implied move 15.14%, run-up 5d +8.9% / 20d -13.7%, 22% off the 52w high. Crowded and building short into a name that pays for beats.

findings.finding: Merge Labs signed a multiyear exclusive license for Butterfly's Poseidon ultrasound-on-chip on ~2026-09-01 (inside Q3) with upfront and milestone licensing payments, hardware purchase commitments and technology-access fees; the Q3 guide ($26-30M, embedded guided at ~$7-8M/quarter) was set on 2026-07-30 before it, and the last comparable signing quarter (Midjourney, Q4 2025) recognised $6.8M in the quarter of signing, so Q3 embedded can land above the $7-8M run-rate and lift total revenue above the ~$29M consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Embedded-driven revenue beats were bought on the print day: Q2 2026 (revenue $32.6M vs ~$28.4-29.2M consensus, embedded $10.8M) +15.07%; Q4 2025 (Midjourney $6.8M in signing quarter) +50.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: No 8-K disclosed the deal value (no Item 1.01), so no estimate can carry it; consensus at $28.8-29.9M sits at or below the top of a guide written before the deal. If priced, consensus would sit above $30M and the stock would not have fallen ~23% from $10.02 (CEO 10b5-1 sale price 2026-10-06) to $7.74 into the print. Revenue is recognised over time by input method (10-Q), which caps how much lands in one quarter.
findings.independence: Midjourney precedent in Q4 2025 call coverage (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/butterfly-network-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-30/ and Q4 2025 transcript https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/02/26/butterfly-bfly-q4-2025-earnings-call-transcript/); embedded run-rate $7-8M +/- $1-2M from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/30/butterfly-bfly-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Inference on timing, not a disclosed number.

findings.finding: Butterfly has beaten revenue consensus four straight quarters (by 1.7% to 21.8%) and beat the top of its own Q2 guide ($27-31M) by $1.6M with $32.6M, raising FY twice (117-121 to 119-123); the Q3 guide of $26-30M is below Q2's actual, a conservative pattern that points to a print above the ~$29M bar.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: a habitual beater's consensus usually drifts above the guide midpoint, and here it has ($28.8-29.9M vs $28M). It is not fully priced if consensus still sits inside the guide while the last quarter cleared the top end.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001804176/000180417626000014/bfly-20260430xexx991.htm) shows $26.5M vs $26.1M consensus and the earlier FY guide $117-121M; Q2 8-K shows the raise. Same company documents.

findings.finding: International revenue fell 14% y/y to $5.0M in Q2, which management attributed in part to orders that slipped into Q3, a timing tailwind to Q3 core revenue on top of a core business that grew only 2% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International was a secondary line on prior prints; no print in the baseline turned on it alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It was said on the call, so it is in the guide; it only adds if the slipped orders are not already inside the $26-30M range. Small for that reason.
findings.independence: 10-Q disaggregation shows international $5.02M vs $5.84M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1804176/000180417626000027/bfly-20260630.htm). Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Since the 2026-07-30 FY guide ($119-123M) the company announced further embedded and enterprise deals that are not in it: Merge Labs (2026-09-01, ongoing licence fees and hardware purchases), Mendaera Focalist compatibility (2026-10-01, Needham values it at ~$25M over time, launching later this year), Bridge Neurotech BCI partnership with early-access and milestone payments (2026-10-06), and a long-term VCOM education alliance (2026-10-13); these support a third FY raise or a firm Q4 rather than a cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two FY raises in 2026 came with +50.65% (Feb, first guide plus Midjourney) and +15.07% (July raise); the April reaffirm went -2.64%.
findings.why_not_priced: None of these deals carried a disclosed dollar value, so no consensus model can add them; the stock fell from ~$10 (2026-10-06) to $7.74 after they were announced, which is not what a priced FY raise looks like. The Merge Labs announcement itself drew a -9.5% session.
findings.independence: Needham initiation coverage (2026-09-22) with the Mendaera ~$25M and Midjourney $300M-by-2030 estimates: https://www.webull.com/news/15622887246988288 . Shares the Merge Labs fact with finding 1 for Q3; this finding counts only its effect on Q4/FY.

findings.finding: Management promised FedRAMP certification 'in the third quarter of 2026' in the Q2 release; no certification announcement was found by 2026-10-28, so the release may report a slip on a VA/federal channel the company has been building.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on a government certification.
findings.why_not_priced: It may simply be announced in the release; absence of a press release is weak evidence, hence the small size and wide band.
findings.independence: GovRAMP/TX-RAMP release (2026-02-10) set the 2026 FedRAMP expectation: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260210884103/en/Butterfly-Network-Achieves-GovRAMP-and-TX-RAMP-Information-Security-Cer . No independent confirmation of a slip.

findings.finding: Q3 adjusted EBITDA was guided to a $6-9M loss against $1.4M in Q2, and the guide names AI-driven supply-chain (memory) shortages and tariffs; GE HealthCare, a direct ultrasound competitor, carries ~$100M of 2026 memory-chip inflation, so the record 71% gross margin may step back and the quality of the print can disappoint even on a revenue beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin durability was the stated reason for the -8.5% day after the Q2 beat (outside that window); Q1 2026 (-2.64%) and earlier prints sold off on persistent losses despite revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The EBITDA step-down is guided and therefore largely priced; the memory-cost transmission to Butterfly is a peer proxy the company called 'minor' so far. Filed small for both reasons.
findings.independence: Butterfly's own Q2 release names 'AI-driven supply chain shortages' as a risk and the 10-Q notes 'increased prices of certain inventory components' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1804176/000180417626000027/bfly-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Short interest rose 6.2% to 33.6M shares (16.2% of float, 6.2 days to cover) at the 2026-10-15 settlement while option open interest is 86% calls (put/call 0.16) and 25d skew is -1.92 (calls bid): a crowded, building short into a name whose last three beats produced +15% to +51% print-day moves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Print-day moves of +31.86%, +50.65% and +15.07% on the last three beats with raised outlooks; short interest was ~14.5% of float at the time of the July print.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, not a fact against it; it adds only convexity to a beat. If shorts were not building, SI would be flat or falling into the print.
findings.independence: Baseline options block (put/call OI 0.16, skew -1.92, sealed 2026-10-28); June settlement 28.7M / 14.5% per Benzinga (https://benzinga.com/quote/BFLY/short-interest).

findings.finding: The core (non-embedded) business grew only 2% y/y in Q2 ($21.85M vs $21.39M) after +10% in Q1, product revenue fell to $15.7M from $16.6M, ASP fell 12% and international fell 14%; if Q3 core is flat again the print rests on lumpy licence revenue, which the market has sold before.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 beat (+15.07% on the day) was given back -8.5% the next session on durability doubts; Q1 2026 core +10% with a small beat went -2.64%.
findings.why_not_priced: The deceleration is in the 10-Q, but consensus and the wire track total revenue and embedded growth; a second flat core quarter would be read as the trend rather than a blip.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary on ASP -12% and VCOM pricing subsidy (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/30/butterfly-bfly-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Same company, different document.

outside_window.finding: Next-generation probe launch guided for early 2027 and Mendaera Focalist commercial ramp; chip-sale revenue would show in 2027 prints.
Company presents at the UBS Global Healthcare Conference on 2026-11-10, after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The lean is up and agrees with the mildly call-bid skew and call-heavy open interest, and cuts against the 20-day run-up (-13.7%) only in that the stock has de-rated without an identified cause, which I do not count as evidence either way.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the positioning finding no longer leans on the ~23% October slide as an 'expectations reset'; resized +1.5 to +1.0.
Lesson 5 / core (absence is not evidence): FedRAMP-slip finding rests on a missing announcement; resized -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the beat-track-record finding is partly priced by consensus sitting above the guide midpoint; resized +1.0 to +0.8.

Lessons 1, 6, 9 checked and left standing: reaction history shows beat-and-raise prints were bought on the day; the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two estimates; the embedded findings are sized net of a flat core, which is filed separately as a negative.
